facts.value: Passes Kirby's fighter object first to ftCo_8009917C. A nonzero result invokes charge-preserving held-shot/effect cleanup. Otherwise it reads input.pressed_buttons: mask 0x200 selects motion 0x19A and refreshes callbacks, then returns; only if that branch is absent can mask 0x80000000 select motion 0x199, clean transient shot/effect state and refresh callbacks. The cleanup does not reset u.kb.xA8.
facts.rationale: Replaces stale input.x668 and held-input wording with the pinned source field while preserving exact masks, numeric destinations and priority.

evidence.why: Current input source and ordered branches.
Charge-preserving cleanup contrasted with explicit full reset.

facts.value: Fighter IASA callback with signature void(Fighter_GObj* gobj). The argument supplies Kirby's Fighter, whose input.pressed_buttons is tested and whose copied-Charge-Shot state is transitioned or cleaned up.
facts.rationale: Retains the exact signature while removing the unsupported continuously held-input description.

evidence.why: Signature, Fighter lookup and pressed-button reads.

facts.value: The common escape check has first priority. If it succeeds, transient Charge Shot cleanup runs. Otherwise pressed_buttons mask 0x200 enters grounded firing state 0x19A and returns after callback setup. Only when that branch is absent can pressed_buttons mask 0x80000000 enter cancel state 0x199, clean the held item/effects and reinstall callbacks. If no condition succeeds, this callback requests no transition. Stored charge is not reset by these cleanup paths.
facts.rationale: Corrects held-button semantics while retaining exact branch priority and charge lifetime.

evidence.why: Cancel and firing state registration with numeric annotations.

facts.value: Handles becoming airborne during Kirby's grounded copied-Charge-Shot cancel phase by selecting ftKb_MS_SsSpecialAirN and restoring copied-special callbacks. This is a transition to the aerial firing state, not a guarantee of projectile firing: cancel cleanup removes the held shot, this collision callback does not create one or arm command 1, and the release helper requires both the command and a retained item.
facts.rationale: Separates action-state selection from actual projectile release and preserves the cancel-to-air exceptional lifetime.

evidence.why: State transition without spawning or arming release.
Actual launch requires command 1 and a retained shot.
